title: Beyond Diagnosis: Structural Stigma, Trauma, and Mental Health Among People Living with HIV in Tunisia
content: HIV-related stigma constitutes a critical structural determinant adversely affecting mental health and treatment outcomes among people living with HIV/AIDS (PLWH) in Tunisia. Rooted in cultural conservatism, legal criminalization, and institutional discrimination, stigma engenders social exclusion, trauma, and internalized shame precipitating depression, anxiety, and treatment non-adherence. This narrative review synthesizes recent epidemiological data showing 0.1% general population prevalence but 13% among MSM, with only 26% testing coverage (Primary Health Department Tunisia, 2024) (Hatem). Situated within trauma, social determinants of health, and public health frameworks, this analysis identifies specific challenges for women and older adults living with HIV. Multisectoral strategies integrating healthcare provider training, legal reform, and culturally-tailored mental health services are essential to mitigate stigma's harms and improve equitable health outcomes in Tunisia.
